title: Teams sign-in fails for part of the Lyon site
scenario: Half of one site is unable to open Teams because one of its two DHCP-issued DNS servers answers almost nothing after a rack move; taking it out of the scope fixes it.

events.title: Teams will not open for half of Lyon
events.text: Bonjour, I am writing for the whole IT desk. Since this morning around 8:30 local time (06:30 UTC I believe) a lot of colleagues at our Lyon site cannot get into Teams: the window opens, spins, then says it could not find the server and offers a Retry button. Retry works for some of them after two or three attempts. We are about 60 people on this floor. The Paris office is perfectly fine, I asked their service desk. I am worried because we have a client workshop at 14:00 and everybody needs Teams for it.

events.title: Re: Teams will not open for half of Lyon
events.text: Hello, thanks for the clear description, and understood about the 14:00 workshop. To get moving I need three things: (1) the exact text of the message on screen, ideally a screenshot of one; (2) the names of three affected users and the UTC moment at which each of them failed; (3) which DNS servers and which proxy the Lyon clients use. If you can also tell me whether anything in the network was touched this week, that would help a lot.

events.title: Re: Teams will not open for half of Lyon
events.text: Screenshot attached (I cannot paste it here). The message says: We couldn't connect, the server name could not be resolved. Error code: caa82ee7. Users: m.leclerc 06:41 UTC, s.bonnet 06:47 UTC, j.garnier 06:52 UTC. Lyon clients get 10.30.4.5 and 10.30.4.6 from DHCP and go out directly, there is no proxy at this site. As for changes: the infrastructure team moved the Lyon DNS service to a new rack on Monday night, but they said it was transparent.

events.title: Sign-in log lookup
events.text: Looked up m.leclerc, s.bonnet and j.garnier in the Entra sign-in logs between 06:30 and 07:00 UTC, interactive and non-interactive. No failed sign-in rows for any of them in that window. The attempts are failing before they get as far as the service.

events.title: Name resolution test from a Lyon PC
events.text: Remote session on a Lyon laptop. Resolved login.microsoftonline.com against 10.30.4.5 and against 10.30.4.6, ten times each. 10.30.4.5: ten answers, all under 20 ms. 10.30.4.6: three answers out of ten, the rest came back SERVFAIL. Same pattern for the CDN host names.

events.title: Findings and a quick fix
events.text: Good news, I think we have it. One of your two Lyon DNS servers, 10.30.4.6, fails to resolve the Microsoft sign-in names most of the time, while 10.30.4.5 is healthy. That fits a new rack. Please ask the infrastructure team to take .6 out of the Lyon DHCP scope right now so that clients only receive .5; leases renew within the hour and restarting Teams will speed it up for people. I will check back at 10:30 UTC with some test sign-ins to confirm.

events.title: Re: Findings and a quick fix
events.text: Done. My colleague removed 10.30.4.6 from the Lyon scope at 08:20 UTC and forced a lease refresh. He found that the forwarder on the new rack still points at the old datacentre resolver, which has been switched off. He will repoint it this afternoon.

events.title: Re: Findings and a quick fix
events.text: It is 10:15 UTC and nobody in Lyon has complained since the scope change. I watched the helpdesk queue and also tried Teams on six different machines myself, all of them signed in at the first attempt.

events.title: Before and after
events.text: Ran 20 sign-ins from three Lyon machines between 10:20 and 10:35 UTC: 20 of 20 succeeded, none slow. Failure notices at the helpdesk since 08:20 UTC: zero. Between 06:30 and 08:20 UTC about a third of attempts had failed.

events.title: Closing note
events.text: Root cause: the forwarder on the new Lyon rack pointed at a decommissioned resolver, so one of the two DNS servers handed out by DHCP could not resolve Microsoft names. Workaround: 10.30.4.6 removed from the scope. Permanent fix is with the infrastructure team, who will repoint the forwarder and confirm that every sign-in host resolves before the server goes back into the scope.
